title: Security & Compliance Operational Guidance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's operational guidance for the primary security and compliance domains required by enterprise customers and auditors: role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging and monitoring, data residency and retention, secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) controls, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence packaging and submission workflows, and a standardized process for risk and exceptions. It is intended for engineering leads, security owners, SREs, and compliance reviewers.

Scope

- Applies to all production and customer-facing control planes, management consoles, and private deployment components (VPC/on-prem).
- Includes hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployment packaging.
- Excludes ephemeral developer sandboxes that are explicitly labeled and isolated; those must follow a reduced control baseline documented separately.

1) RBAC and Authentication

Summary
- Use least-privilege RBAC as the default access model across all Redwood services. Authentication is handled via federated SSO for corporate access and token-based mutual auth for service-to-service interactions.

Roles and Permissions
- Roles (examples):
  - security-admin: full configuration, compliance reporting, and exception approvals.
  - platform-admin: cluster and infra provisioning, IAM role mappings.
  - oncall-eng: read/write runbook and emergency scaling operations.
  - dev-readonly: repo and dashboard read-only access.
  - customer-admin: scoped to customer-owned resources in Private deployments.

Permissions mapping (sample table)
| Role | Resource Scope | Common Actions | Approval Required |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| security-admin | Global | manage-policies, view-audit | Exec security |
| platform-admin | Prod clusters | deploy, scale, rotate-keys | Sec review on key rotate |
| oncall-eng | Project | change-routes, restart-services | Post-incident review |

Authentication and SSO
- Corporate access: SAML 2.0 / OIDC through identity providers (Okta, Azure AD). Enforce:
  - MFA required for all interactive logins.
  - Passwordless options allowed where supported.
  - Session timeout: 8 hours for privileged roles, 24 hours for low-privilege read-only roles.
- Service-to-service: mTLS with short-lived certs (maximum TTL 24h) and JWT-based signed service tokens for API calls.

Access Review and Certification
1. Quarterly entitlement reviews for all high privilege roles (security-admin, platform-admin).
2. Automated weekly report of privileged role assignment changes sent to security-operations@redwood.ai.
3. On employee offboarding, deprovisioning must complete within 2 hours of termination event.

2) Audit Logging and Monitoring

Objectives
- Provide immutable, queryable audit trails for config changes, access events, and data export requests.
- Enable timely detection of suspicious activity with alerts integrated into PagerDuty and the security console.

Logging Requirements
- Events captured: authentication success/failure, CSRF/permission-denied events, policy changes, role assignments, API key usage, data export/download actions, and KMS/HSM key operations.
- Log retention: 1 year hot search index, 7 years cold archive (encrypted).
- Format and schema: JSON structured logs with stable fields: timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_id, outcome, request_id, ip_address, user_agent.
- Tamper resistance: logs written to append-only backed store with versioned checksums and write-once object storage for archival.

Alerting and Detection
- High-priority alerts (PagerDuty): multiple failed privileged auth within 15 minutes, unexpected key rotations, deletion of audit archives, bulk data export by non-admin.
- Medium alerts: anomalous IPs, privilege elevation, policy change outside maintenance windows.

Log Access and Queries
- Access to raw logs restricted to security and SRE by default. Data access requests from engineering require ticket and justification.
- Standard queries and dashboards published in dashboards-and-alerts with playbooks for common investigations.

3) Data Residency and Retention

Data Classification
- Categories: PII, Customer Data (unstructured model inputs/outputs), System Telemetry, Operational Metadata, and Backups.

Residency Controls
- Region-binding: Customer data must be stored only in approved regions per contract (e.g., eu-west-1 for EU customers).
- Private deployments: customers can designate local on-prem storage endpoints; Redwood config enforces routing through regional gateways.

Retention Policy (default)
- Customer Data (short-term inference logs): 30 days hot, opt-in extended retention up to 365 days by contract.
- Audit logs: 1 year hot, 7 years archive.
- Backups & artifacts: 90 days for ephemeral snapshots, 7 years for legally required backups.
- Telemetry and metrics: 90 days detailed, 5 years aggregated.

Data Deletion and Erasure Requests
1. Data subject/ customer erasure requests routed to privacy@redwood.ai.
2. Erasure steps: identify data locations, revoke replication, run secure deletion on object store, verify with deletion job ID, and update evidence ticket. Target SLA: 30 days for complete verification.

4) Secure SDLC

Policy Highlights
- All code changes must pass CI checks: static analysis, dependency scanning (SCA), unit/integration tests, and container image vulnerability scans.
- Mandatory threat model review for services that process customer data or call external model providers.
- Secrets management: no secrets in repo; use central Vault (HashiCorp Vault) with rotation policy (default 90 days).

CI/CD Controls
- Branch protections and required approvals: at least 2 approvers for changes to production configs and infra-as-code.
- Canary deploy and automated rollback thresholds: 0.5% error increase or latency >2x baseline triggers auto-rollback.
- Signed artifacts: build system signs artifacts; signature verified by deploy pipeline.

Developer Security Training
- Annual secure-coding training required for all engineers, with targeted modules for infra and runtime teams.

5) Incident Response - Security Procedures

Runbook Summary
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev 1 (Critical): Active data exfiltration, production outage affecting >20% customers, or confirmed key compromise.
  - Sev 2 (High): Partial outage, potential credential compromise, or significant security-sensitive misconfiguration.
  - Sev 3 (Medium): Degraded service, non-production leak, or low-impact vulnerability.

Immediate Actions (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage and classify severity; notify incident commander and on-call security.
2. Containment: isolate affected services (network ACLs, revoke tokens, rotate keys if evidence of compromise).
3. Preserve evidence: create forensic snapshots, enable verbose audit logging, and record all actions in the Incident ticket.

Investigation and Remediation
- Forensic timeline must include: initial alert time, actor IDs, IP addresses, commands executed, and object IDs.
- Remediation plan must include root cause, fix checklist, postmortem owner, and customer communication plan.

Post-Incident Requirements
- Postmortem published within 7 business days for Sev1/Sev2 incidents. Redacted public summary for customers within 3 business days of incident containment.
- Regulatory notifications: evaluate GDPR breach criteria and notify Data Protection Authorities within 72 hours if applicable.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Objective
- Provide a repeatable, auditable workflow to package requested evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and customer security assessments.

Evidence Packaging Steps
1. Intake: security-gating receives request via security-requests@redwood.ai and creates a ticket with scope and due date.
2. Evidence collection: owners pull artifacts: access logs, policy docs, SSO snapshots, key rotation records, and configuration manifests.
3. Validation: evidence checked against evidence checklist.
4. Packaging: create ZIP of artifacts with manifest.json (hashes and signer) and upload to secure evidence bucket.
5. Delivery: share signed link with auditor or customer and log delivery event in audit system.

SLA and Ownership
- Standard SLA: 10 business days for SOC 2 or ISO requests, 5 business days for customer security questionnaires where artifacts already exist.
- Owners: security-ops owns packaging; system owners provide artifacts within SLA.

7) Risk and Exceptions Process

When to request an exception
- Exceptions requested when an approved control cannot be implemented without unacceptable business impact, or a compensating control is proposed. Examples: legacy customer integrations, hardware constraints in on-prem deployments.

Exception Request Procedure
1. Submit exception request via internal ticketing template with: scope, risk statement, compensating controls, compensating monitoring, proposed end date, and owner.
2. Security reviews risk and assigns residual risk rating (low/medium/high).
3. Risk committee decision required for medium/high residual risk; approval includes required compensating controls and review cadence.
4. Approved exceptions are recorded in the risk registry with automated reminders for re-evaluation.

Controls and Monitoring for Exceptions
- Monitoring baseline: increased logging, weekly exception-specific queries, and monthly review with security-ops.
- Maximum exception duration: 12 months. Extensions require renewed risk committee approval.

Ownership, Contacts, and Escalation
- Document owner: Security Operations (security-ops@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: Head of Security (head-of-security@redwood.ai), CISO (ciso@redwood.ai)
- Evidence and audit contact: compliance@redwood.ai

Appendix: Example Commands, Policy Snippets, and Templates

Example: list privileged role bindings (kubectl example)
1) kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, subjects:.subjects, roleRef:.roleRef}'

Example: evidence manifest.json (manifest is a single-line JSON listing file names and SHA256 hashes)
- manifest.json example (stored in evidence package): {"files": ["audit-2027-11.log", "policy-rbac-v2.pdf"], "hashes": ["<sha256-audit-2027-11>", "<sha256-policy>"]}

Template: exception request checklist
- Title, Owner, Affected systems, Duration, Compensating controls, Monitoring plan, Re-evaluation date, Approvals.

Review and Revision
- This guidance will be reviewed annually or after any Sev1 incident. Any changes to regional laws or customer contractual obligations will trigger an out-of-cycle review.

References
- Internal: dashboards-and-alerts RBAC dashboards, incident-response/runbooks, security-and-compliance controlbook.
- External: SOC 2 Common Criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A, GDPR Article 33 (breach notification).
